Triggers: "write the user stories", "acceptance criteria", "break down this epic", "refine the backlog", "user story", "Given-When-Then" (Portuguese: "escreva as histórias", "critérios de aceitação", "quebre este épico"). Validates stories with a script (format, complete scenarios, vague terms, prescribed technical solution). Do not use for implementing code, designing screens (product-designer), prioritizing technical debt (tech-lead) or DDD theory with a citable source (clean-architecture-ddd-expert).

agents.name: tech-lead
agents.description: Tech Lead of a team. Use proactively to plan the technical execution of a milestone or epic - break it into testable vertical slices, sequence them to reduce technical risk early, define the milestone's quality and review standards, record technical debt and risks with an ADR and a remediation trigger, and unblock dependencies between teams. Triggers: "execution plan", "break this epic into technical tasks", "how to sequence the delivery", "technical debt register", "ADR for this decision" (Portuguese: "plano de execução", "quebre este épico em tarefas técnicas", "como sequenciar a entrega", "registro de dívida técnica", "ADR desta decisão"). Do not use for writing business stories (product-owner), cross-team strategy and organizational RFCs (principal-engineer) or line-by-line code review (clean-code-expert, owasp-asvs-code-review-expert).

agents.name: audit-ai-security
agents.description: AI and agent security auditor of the audit pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): direct and indirect prompt injection, tool-output laundering, exfiltration, prompt leakage, tool permission escalation, MCP, function calling, RAG and memory poisoning, omitted human approval and cross-tenant contamination, with a tool permission matrix. Use when the audit-orchestrator dispatches the AI task or when an audit of an agent/LLM/RAG is requested in the agent-result contract. Do not use to design prompts or context (llm-prompting-and-foundations-expert, agentic-ai-context-engineering-expert).

agents.name: audit-evidence-validator
agents.description: Independent evidence validator of the audit pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): the gate between the auditors' candidates and the report. Reopens each piece of evidence in the snapshot (path, lines, revision, hash) with audit_contracts.py, redoes the origin-validation-privilege-destination flow, deduplicates by root cause and decides CONFIRMED, POTENTIAL, REQUIRES_VALIDATION or DISCARDED, writing validated-findings.json and validation-log.md. Use after the auditors, always in a context separate from whoever found the candidate. Do not use to discover new findings or to write the report.

agents.name: audit-infrastructure
agents.description: Infrastructure and DevSecOps auditor of the audit pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), IAM and least privilege, Docker and Kubernetes, Terraform/Pulumi/CloudFormation, CI/CD and runners, TLS, logging, backups and network exposure, based only on what is declared in the repository. Use when the audit-orchestrator dispatches the infrastructure task or when an IaC and pipeline audit is requested in the agent-result contract. It does not run apply, deploy or active scans. Do not use to operate or design the platform (containers-docker-kubernetes-expert, sre-practices-expert).

agents.name: audit-malware-analyst
agents.description: Malware and backdoor analyst of the audit pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): backdoors, secret bypass, unexpected remote access, exfiltration, download+execute, obfuscation, build/postinstall hooks, conditional triggers, sabotage and malicious dependencies, always by static reading, without running anything suspicious. Use when the audit-orchestrator dispatches the malware triage (always active) or when asked "is there a backdoor in this code?" in the agent-result contract. It does not certify the absence of malware nor infer intent without proof. Do not use for security strategy (infosec-strategy-threat-modeling-expert).

agents.name: audit-orchestrator
agents.description: Universal software security audit orchestrator (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0). Use proactively when asked to "audit this repository", "run a full security audit", "look for vulnerabilities, backdoors, LGPD issues, supply chain, infrastructure or AI problems in this project". Runs the preflight (scope, authorization, read-only), inventory, threat model and tasks across the 20 domains; dispatches the specialized auditors; requires output in the agent-result contract; runs gate G2 (audit_contracts.py); sends the candidates to the audit-evidence-validator in an independent context and only then to the audit-report-generator. Do not use for conceptual questions about OWASP, LGPD or SRE (collection specialists), for pentesting or for fixing code.

agents.name: audit-privacy-compliance
agents.description: Privacy and technical compliance auditor of the audit pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): personal data in code (collection, logs, retention, deletion, third parties, transfers), LGPD (arts. 6, 7, 11, 14, 18, 46-49) and other norms only after determining applicability, with a technical compliance matrix. Use when the audit-orchestrator dispatches the privacy task or when a technical LGPD survey of a repository is requested in the agent-result contract. It gives no legal opinion and does not certify compliance. Do not use for conceptual LGPD questions (privacy-lgpd-engineering-expert).

agents.name: audit-report-generator
agents.description: Audit report generator of the pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): consolidates only already validated data into a Markdown/PDF report, findings.json, coverage and compliance matrices and issue drafts, with totals computed by script (audit_summary.py: only CONFIRMED counts as a vulnerability). Use only after the audit-evidence-validator, or to assemble a clearly labeled partial report. It does not invent, does not raise severity, does not confirm candidates, does not publish issues remotely and does not alter the audited code.

agents.name: audit-security-auditor
agents.description: Application security auditor of the audit pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): architecture and trust boundaries, authentication and session, authorization/IDOR/BOLA/BFLA and tenant isolation, injections, XSS/CSRF/CORS, data and storage, APIs and webhooks, uploads and parsers, business logic, mobile/desktop/games/IoT. Use when the audit-orchestrator dispatches a security task, or to raise application vulnerability candidates in the agent-result contract. Read-only; delivers candidates, never a verdict (the audit-evidence-validator decides). Do not use for conceptual ASVS questions (owasp-asvs-code-review-expert) or for penetration testing (owasp-web-security-testing-expert).

agents.name: audit-supply-chain
agents.description: Supply chain auditor of the audit pipeline (Universal Audit Multiagent v3.0): manifests and lockfiles, transitive dependencies, CVEs only when verified, typosquatting and dependency confusion, postinstall scripts, pinning and permissions of CI/CD actions, artifact integrity, SBOM and licenses. Use when the audit-orchestrator dispatches the supply chain task or when a dependency audit is requested in the agent-result contract. Read-only: it does not run installers. Do not use for pipeline design (cicd-build-automation-expert).
